text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141. @
ALL PAPERS
- Hungary was granted two loans each worth DM 250 million from Baden-Wurttemberg and Bavaria yesterday. The documents were signed in the presence of visiting Prime Minister Gyula Horn.
- President Arpad Goncz delivered a lecture on 1956 yesterday at the Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm.

- The Slovak Foreign Ministry released a statement Wednesday critical of the protest expressed by the Hungarian Foreign Ministry spokesman a day earlier against the new house rule in the Slovak Parliament. @

- Constitutional committee members expressed shock and outrage yesterday following a hearing of State Privatisation and Holding Co president Imre Szokai regarding the controversy surrounding a lawyer who has received over HUF 300 milion this year for her work in negotiating land claims with local governments.
- The union representing public service institutions said it lays claim to a 20 percent salary increase in 1997.
- Parliament's two committees yesterday approved the nomination of Gyorgy Gillyan to the post of administrative state secretary at the Ministry of Industry and Trade. @
NEPSZABADSAG

- German energy investors are inclined to accept a compromise solution if the Hungarian cabinet were to increase energy prices to a lesser extent than would allow companies to offset costs and maintain profits necessary for development projects, said a representative of one foreign investor.
- Jean-Marie le Pen, president of France's far-right National Front party, will deliver a speech at the October 27 rally of the Hungarian Justice and Life Party. @
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- GE Capital and the EBRD may request the Minister of Finance to buy back their shares in Budapest Bank plus 3 percent interest at any time before May 15, 1999, according to a "secret" clause in the sales agreement signed last December.

- The Board of Directors of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. has spent more money on reorganising (upgrading) state-owned companies than the limit stipulated by the budget law, said budget committee head Laszlo Keller. @
- In his first programme speech to staff members, MTV president Istvan Petak pledged to phase out 2,000 staff members and announced the dismissal of 500 persons in the labour pool.
- The privatisation of the Hungarian Electricity Works has attracted interest from several multinational consortiums.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. has approved a plan to sell 11.66 per cent of BorsodChem shares through a closed offering.
- A four-day international conference entitled Women in the Heart of Europe opens with a ceremony in Parliament today. @
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Today this paper reports further details of the 1997 draft budget submitted to Parliament.
- Bank of America has withdrawn from the privatisation of Magyar Hitel Bank.
- Rabobank Hungaria Rt., the subsidiary of the Dutch concern Rabobank International, has submitted an application for a banking licence to the State Banking Supervision. @
NEPSZAVA
- Pharmaceuticals are expected to cost 15 percent more as of January 1, 1997.
